objects.definition:
typedef struct redisReply {
    int type; /* REDIS_REPLY_* */
    long long integer; /* The integer when type is REDIS_REPLY_INTEGER */
    double dval; /* The double when type is REDIS_REPLY_DOUBLE */
    size_t len; /* Length of string */
    char *str; /* Used for REDIS_REPLY_ERROR, REDIS_REPLY_STRING
                  REDIS_REPLY_VERB, REDIS_REPLY_DOUBLE (in additional to dval),
                  and REDIS_REPLY_BIGNUM. */
    char vtype[4]; /* Used for REDIS_REPLY_VERB, contains the null
                      terminated 3 character content type, such as "txt". */
    size_t elements; /* number of elements, for REDIS_REPLY_ARRAY */
    struct redisReply **element; /* elements vector for REDIS_REPLY_ARRAY */
} redisReply;
objects.description: Heap-allocated RESP reply object returned by redisCommand/redisGetReply. Holds type and payload for all RESP2/RESP3 variants including integers, strings, arrays, verbatim strings (vtype), doubles, and big numbers. Free with freeReplyObject unless using custom allocators. Elements points to an array of redisReply* for aggregate types.
Enumeration of underlying transport used by a redisContext: TCP/IP, Unix domain socket, or an already-open user-provided file descriptor.

objects.definition:
#ifndef _WIN32
typedef int redisFD;
#define REDIS_INVALID_FD -1
#else
#ifdef _WIN64
typedef unsigned long long redisFD; /* SOCKET = 64-bit UINT_PTR */
#else
typedef unsigned long redisFD;      /* SOCKET = 32-bit UINT_PTR */
#endif
#define REDIS_INVALID_FD ((redisFD)(~0)) /* INVALID_SOCKET */
#endif
objects.description: Platform-dependent file-descriptor/socket handle type used by hiredis for I/O (signed int on POSIX; unsigned SOCKET-sized integer on Windows). Use REDIS_INVALID_FD to denote an invalid handle.

Configuration struct for establishing a connection. Selects transport via type and endpoint union, sets options and timeouts, and allows user privdata and PUSH callbacks. Initialize with REDIS_OPTIONS_SET_TCP/UNIX/PRIVDATA macros or manually. Pass to redisConnectWithOptions.
Virtual function table for redisContext I/O and lifecycle hooks (close, read/write, async operations). Typically set internally (e.g., for SSL) rather than by users.

Synchronous hiredis connection context encapsulating socket/transport, timeouts, buffers, reader, and error state. Created by redisConnect* APIs and freed with redisFree or redisFreeKeepFd. Manages IO and can hold user privdata and optional PUSH callback.

objects.definition: struct redisSsl;
objects.description: Opaque forward declaration for SSL context used internally by hiredis when SSL is enabled. Not defined in this header; managed internally. Details unknown.

objects.definition: typedef void (redisPushFn)(void *, void *);
objects.description: Callback function type for handling RESP3 PUSH messages in synchronous contexts. First argument is user/context pointer, second is reply pointer. Exact semantics depend on registration site.

objects.definition: typedef void (redisAsyncPushFn)(struct redisAsyncContext *, void *);
objects.description: Callback function type for handling RESP3 PUSH messages in async contexts. Takes async context and reply pointer. The async context is forward-declared here.
Protocol reader type referenced by this header (declared in read.h). Not defined here; definition resides elsewhere. Used by redisContext and related APIs.

objects.definition: typedef void (redisCallbackFn)(struct redisAsyncContext*, void*, void*);
objects.description: Function type for per-command reply callbacks invoked with the async context, the reply object, and user privdata. Exact reply type depends on hiredis; details not specified here.
Node in a singly linked list holding a reply callback, subscription bookkeeping fields, and user privdata. Used to dispatch command or subscription replies in async mode.
Container maintaining head/tail pointers for a queue of redisCallback nodes. Used for regular replies and pub/sub callbacks.

objects.definition: typedef void (redisDisconnectCallback)(const struct redisAsyncContext*, int status);
objects.description: Function type invoked on disconnect events with the async context and a status code (REDIS_OK or REDIS_ERR).

objects.definition: typedef void (redisConnectCallback)(const struct redisAsyncContext*, int status);
objects.description: Function type invoked when the first write event indicates the connection is established; receives the async context and status.

objects.definition: typedef void (redisConnectCallbackNC)(struct redisAsyncContext *, int status);
objects.description: Non-const variant of the connect callback type; receives a mutable async context pointer and status.

objects.definition: typedef void(redisTimerCallback)(void *timer, void *privdata);
objects.description: Function type for timer callbacks scheduled by the event layer. Takes an opaque timer handle and user privdata.

Primary async connection context for hiredis. Embeds a redisContext, error fields, user data hooks, event loop integration callbacks, connect/disconnect callbacks, reply queues, addressing info, subscription state, and an optional RESP3 PUSH handler. Constructed via redisAsyncConnect* APIs and freed with redisAsyncFree/redisAsyncDisconnect.

Task node used by the Redis protocol reader to track parsing state for the current reply hierarchy (arrays, maps, etc.). Each task represents one reply element, keeps its type, element count for containers, index in parent, a user object placeholder, and links to its parent task plus user privdata.
Vtable of callbacks the parser uses to construct reply objects for each RESP type and to free them. Applications provide implementations to map parsed data to their own reply representation.

Stateful RESP protocol parser. Maintains input buffer, parsing position, task stack, and callback table for constructing reply objects. err/errstr report errors. Applications feed bytes and retrieve constructed replies. privdata is user-defined context passed through tasks/callbacks.

objects.definition: struct ssl_st;
objects.description: Forward declaration of the OpenSSL SSL structure. Only referenced here for API interop; the actual definition resides in OpenSSL headers. Incomplete type; details unknown in this header.

objects.definition: typedef struct redisSSLContext redisSSLContext;
objects.description: Opaque wrapper around an OpenSSL SSL_CTX used to configure and initiate SSL/TLS for hiredis without directly invoking OpenSSL. The struct is intentionally not defined here; it is managed via the provided API.

objects.definition:
typedef enum {
    REDIS_SSL_CTX_NONE = 0,                     /* No Error */
    REDIS_SSL_CTX_CREATE_FAILED,                /* Failed to create OpenSSL SSL_CTX */
    REDIS_SSL_CTX_CERT_KEY_REQUIRED,            /* Client cert and key must both be specified or skipped */
    REDIS_SSL_CTX_CA_CERT_LOAD_FAILED,          /* Failed to load CA Certificate or CA Path */
    REDIS_SSL_CTX_CLIENT_CERT_LOAD_FAILED,      /* Failed to load client certificate */
    REDIS_SSL_CTX_CLIENT_DEFAULT_CERT_FAILED,   /* Failed to set client default certificate directory */
    REDIS_SSL_CTX_PRIVATE_KEY_LOAD_FAILED,      /* Failed to load private key */
    REDIS_SSL_CTX_OS_CERTSTORE_OPEN_FAILED,     /* Failed to open system certificate store */
    REDIS_SSL_CTX_OS_CERT_ADD_FAILED            /* Failed to add CA certificates obtained from system to the SSL context */
} redisSSLContextError;
objects.description: Enumeration of possible errors returned when creating an SSL context via redisCreateSSLContext or redisCreateSSLContextWithOptions. Values describe specific initialization failures.
Options structure for configuring SSL context creation, including CA file/path, client cert/key, SNI server name, and verification mode flags. Passed to redisCreateSSLContextWithOptions.

functions.name: redisReaderCreate
functions.description: Allocates and returns a new redisReader used to parse RESP replies from a byte stream. Typically used internally by redisContext but can be used directly to feed protocol bytes and extract replies.
requirements: Caller must check the return value for NULL to detect allocation failure.
Caller is responsible for freeing the reader via the corresponding redisReader destroy function (not defined in this header; typically redisReaderFree) once done.

functions.name: freeReplyObject
functions.description: Frees a reply object previously returned by hiredis (e.g., from redisCommand/redisGetReply). Safe deallocation of the hierarchical reply structure.
requirements: The reply argument must be a pointer returned by hiredis reply-producing APIs (e.g., redisCommand/redisGetReply).
Do not use the reply after calling this function.
Behavior for reply == NULL is unknown from this header; the caller should avoid passing NULL unless confirmed safe.

functions.name: redisvFormatCommand
functions.signature: int redisvFormatCommand(char **target, const char *format, va_list ap);
functions.description: Formats a Redis command using a printf-like format string and a va_list, serializing it into the RESP protocol. On success, writes an allocated buffer pointer to *target and returns the buffer length.
requirements: target must be a valid non-NULL pointer to a char*; on success *target will point to a newly allocated buffer that must be freed with redisFreeCommand.
format must be a valid hiredis command format string matching the provided arguments in ap.
Caller must check the integer return value: a negative value indicates an error (exact error codes not specified here).
The lifetime of data referenced by ap must be valid during formatting only; the formatted command is self-contained afterward.

functions.name: redisFormatCommand
functions.description: Formats a Redis command using a printf-like format string and variadic arguments, serializing it into the RESP protocol. On success, sets *target to an allocated buffer and returns its length.
requirements: target must be a valid non-NULL pointer to a char*; on success *target must be freed with redisFreeCommand.
format must be a valid hiredis command format string matching the provided variadic arguments.
Caller must check the integer return value: a negative value indicates an error (exact error codes not specified here).

functions.name: redisFormatCommandArgv
functions.signature: long long redisFormatCommandArgv(char **target, int argc, const char **argv, const size_t *argvlen);
functions.description: Formats a Redis command from an argument vector (argc/argv), serializing it into the RESP protocol. On success, sets *target to an allocated buffer and returns the buffer length.
requirements: target must be a valid non-NULL pointer to a char*; on success *target must be freed with redisFreeCommand.
argc specifies the number of arguments in argv; it should be non-negative and consistent with argv/argvlen lengths (exact constraints not stated here).
argv must point to argc argument strings; if argvlen is non-NULL, each length corresponds to the respective argv entry.
If argvlen is NULL, the function will treat argv strings as null-terminated (behavior inferred from typical API; exact details not stated here).
Caller must check the return value: a negative value indicates an error.

functions.name: redisFormatSdsCommandArgv
functions.signature: long long redisFormatSdsCommandArgv(hisds *target, int argc, const char ** argv, const size_t *argvlen);
functions.description: Formats a Redis command from an argument vector (argc/argv) into an SDS string (hisds). On success, writes the allocated SDS to *target and returns its length.
requirements: target must be a valid non-NULL pointer to an hisds handle; on success *target must be freed with redisFreeSdsCommand.
argc specifies the number of arguments; it should match the number of entries in argv and argvlen (if provided).
argv must point to argc argument strings; if argvlen is non-NULL, each length corresponds to the respective argv entry.
Caller must check the return value: a negative value indicates an error.

functions.name: redisFreeCommand
functions.description: Frees a command buffer previously allocated by a redisFormat* function that returned a char*-based buffer.
requirements: cmd must be a buffer previously returned via redisvFormatCommand/redisFormatCommand/redisFormatCommandArgv.
Do not use the buffer after freeing it.
Behavior for cmd == NULL is unknown from this header; avoid passing NULL unless confirmed safe.

functions.name: redisFreeSdsCommand
functions.description: Frees an SDS command buffer previously allocated by redisFormatSdsCommandArgv.
requirements: cmd must be an hisds previously returned via redisFormatSdsCommandArgv.
Do not use the SDS after freeing it.
Behavior for a null/empty handle is unknown from this header.

functions.name: redisConnectWithOptions
functions.description: Creates a new Redis connection using the supplied redisOptions (TCP, Unix socket, or an existing file descriptor) and returns a redisContext representing the connection.
requirements: options must point to an initialized redisOptions struct with a valid type and corresponding endpoint fields set (e.g., TCP ip/port, Unix path, or fd).
If connect_timeout/command_timeout are provided, they should point to valid struct timeval objects for the duration of the call; options may be copied internally.
Caller must check the returned context for connection errors (c->err/errstr) and for NULL on allocation failure.
The returned context must be freed with redisFree or redisFreeKeepFd.

functions.name: redisConnect
functions.description: Creates a blocking TCP connection to a Redis server at ip:port and returns a redisContext.
requirements: ip must point to a valid null-terminated address string; interpretation of numeric vs hostname is library-defined.
port must identify the server port; valid range is not specified in this header.
Caller must check the returned context for errors and for NULL on allocation failure.
The returned context must be freed with redisFree or redisFreeKeepFd.

functions.name: redisConnectWithTimeout
functions.signature: redisContext *redisConnectWithTimeout(const char *ip, int port, const struct timeval tv);
functions.description: Creates a TCP connection to a Redis server at ip:port with a connect timeout specified by tv, and returns a redisContext.
requirements: ip must point to a valid null-terminated address string.
tv specifies the connect timeout; exact field constraints are not specified here.
Caller must check the returned context for errors and for NULL on allocation failure.
The returned context must be freed with redisFree or redisFreeKeepFd.

functions.name: redisConnectNonBlock
functions.description: Initiates a non-blocking TCP connection to a Redis server at ip:port and returns a redisContext configured for non-blocking I/O.
requirements: ip must point to a valid null-terminated address string.
Caller must integrate the context’s fd with an event loop and use hiredis non-blocking APIs to complete I/O.
Caller must check the returned context for errors and for NULL on allocation failure.
The returned context must be freed with redisFree or redisFreeKeepFd.

functions.name: redisConnectBindNonBlock
functions.signature: redisContext *redisConnectBindNonBlock(const char *ip, int port, const char *source_addr);
functions.description: Initiates a non-blocking TCP connection to ip:port, binding the local socket to source_addr before connecting, and returns a redisContext.
requirements: ip and source_addr must point to valid null-terminated address strings.
Caller must integrate the context’s fd with an event loop and use non-blocking APIs to complete I/O.
Caller must check the returned context for errors and for NULL on allocation failure.
The returned context must be freed with redisFree or redisFreeKeepFd.

functions.name: redisConnectBindNonBlockWithReuse
functions.signature: redisContext *redisConnectBindNonBlockWithReuse(const char *ip, int port, const char *source_addr);
functions.description: Like redisConnectBindNonBlock but configures the socket with SO_REUSEADDR prior to bind(), helping in cases like EADDRNOTAVAIL during reconnects. Returns a non-blocking redisContext.
requirements: ip and source_addr must point to valid null-terminated address strings.
Caller must integrate the context’s fd with an event loop and use non-blocking APIs to complete I/O.
Caller must check the returned context for errors and for NULL on allocation failure.
The returned context must be freed with redisFree or redisFreeKeepFd.

functions.name: redisConnectUnix
functions.description: Creates a blocking connection to a Redis server over a Unix domain socket at the given filesystem path and returns a redisContext.
requirements: path must point to a valid null-terminated filesystem path for a Unix domain socket.
Caller must check the returned context for errors and for NULL on allocation failure.
The returned context must be freed with redisFree or redisFreeKeepFd.

functions.name: redisConnectUnixWithTimeout
functions.signature: redisContext *redisConnectUnixWithTimeout(const char *path, const struct timeval tv);
functions.description: Creates a connection to a Redis server over a Unix domain socket with a connect timeout specified by tv, and returns a redisContext.
requirements: path must point to a valid null-terminated filesystem path.
tv specifies the connect timeout; exact constraints are not specified here.
Caller must check the returned context for errors and for NULL on allocation failure.
The returned context must be freed with redisFree or redisFreeKeepFd.

functions.name: redisConnectUnixNonBlock
functions.description: Initiates a non-blocking Unix domain socket connection to a Redis server at the given path and returns a redisContext.
requirements: path must point to a valid null-terminated filesystem path.
Caller must integrate the context’s fd with an event loop and use non-blocking APIs to complete I/O.
Caller must check the returned context for errors and for NULL on allocation failure.
The returned context must be freed with redisFree or redisFreeKeepFd.

functions.name: redisConnectFd
functions.description: Wraps an already-open file descriptor (or SOCKET on Windows) in a redisContext for communicating with a Redis server using that descriptor.
requirements: fd must be a valid, open, connected socket compatible with Redis protocol I/O.
Caller must ensure the descriptor’s blocking mode matches the intended hiredis usage (blocking or non-blocking).
Caller must check the returned context for errors and for NULL on allocation failure.
The returned context must be freed with redisFree or redisFreeKeepFd. Ownership of fd after redisFreeKeepFd depends on which free function is used.

functions.name: redisReconnect
functions.description: Re-establishes the connection represented by c using the original connection parameters saved in the context. Returns REDIS_OK on success or REDIS_ERR on failure.
requirements: c must be a valid redisContext previously created by a connect function.
Callers should check the integer return value to detect success/failure and inspect c->err/errstr on failure.
Context flags are reused unmodified; host/ip/path, timeouts, and bind address are reused as originally configured.

functions.name: redisSetPushCallback
functions.description: Sets a RESP3 PUSH message handler callback for the given context and returns the previous callback pointer.
requirements: c must be a valid redisContext.
fn must point to a function matching redisPushFn(void *, void *); whether NULL is allowed to clear the callback is not specified here.
Caller should store or ignore the returned previous callback as needed.

functions.name: redisSetTimeout
functions.signature: int redisSetTimeout(redisContext *c, const struct timeval tv);
functions.description: Sets the command timeout on the given context. Returns an integer status (exact values not specified here).
requirements: c must be a valid redisContext.
tv specifies the desired timeout; exact constraints and error codes are not specified here.
Caller should check the return value to ensure the timeout was applied.

functions.name: redisEnableKeepAlive
functions.description: Enables TCP keepalive on the connection using a default interval (HIREDIS_KEEPALIVE_INTERVAL). Returns an integer status (exact values not specified here).
requirements: c must be a valid redisContext with an underlying TCP socket.
Caller should check the return value for success/failure.

functions.name: redisEnableKeepAliveWithInterval
functions.description: Enables TCP keepalive on the connection with a custom interval in seconds. Returns an integer status (exact values not specified here).
requirements: c must be a valid redisContext with an underlying TCP socket.
interval is expressed in seconds; acceptable range and validation are not specified here.
Caller should check the return value for success/failure.

functions.name: redisSetTcpUserTimeout
functions.description: Sets the TCP_USER_TIMEOUT (if supported) on the connection to the specified timeout value. Returns an integer status (exact values not specified here).
requirements: c must be a valid redisContext with an underlying TCP socket.
timeout units and valid range are not specified in this header.
Caller should check the return value for success/failure.

functions.name: redisFree
functions.description: Frees a redisContext and associated resources, closing the underlying socket. Any user-provided privdata will be freed via its destructor if configured.
requirements: c must be a redisContext previously returned by a connect function; passing NULL behavior is not specified here.
After this call, the context pointer must not be used.
If the caller needs to keep the underlying fd open, use redisFreeKeepFd instead.

functions.name: redisFreeKeepFd
functions.description: Frees a redisContext but keeps the underlying socket/file descriptor open and returns it to the caller.
requirements: c must be a redisContext previously returned by a connect function; passing NULL behavior is not specified here.
The returned descriptor becomes the caller’s responsibility to close/manage.
After this call, the context pointer must not be used.

functions.name: redisBufferRead
functions.description: Reads pending data from the socket into hiredis’s read buffer and feeds the protocol reader. Typically used in non-blocking mode to accumulate replies.
requirements: c must be a valid redisContext with an open connection.
Caller should check the return value for success/failure (exact semantics not specified here).
In non-blocking usage, integrate with an event loop to call this when the socket is readable.

functions.name: redisBufferWrite
functions.description: Attempts to flush the output buffer to the socket. Sets *done to 1 when all output has been written, otherwise 0. Typically used in non-blocking mode when the socket is writable.
requirements: c must be a valid redisContext with an open connection.
done should point to an int to receive completion status; whether NULL is allowed is not specified here—pass a valid pointer to be safe.
Caller should check the return value for success/failure (exact semantics not specified here).

functions.name: redisGetReply
functions.description: Retrieves the next available reply. In blocking mode, flushes pending output and reads until a reply is available; in non-blocking mode, returns unconsumed replies if available. On success, *reply receives a reply object pointer (to be freed with freeReplyObject).
requirements: c must be a valid redisContext.
reply must be a non-NULL pointer to a void* variable to receive the reply pointer.
Caller must free the returned reply with freeReplyObject unless automatic reply free is enabled (see options/flags).
Caller must check the integer return value for success/failure (exact values not specified here).

functions.name: redisGetReplyFromReader
functions.description: Parses and returns a reply from the context’s internal reader without performing any socket I/O. Useful after feeding data via redisBufferRead or custom readers.
requirements: c must be a valid redisContext.
reply must be a non-NULL pointer to a void* variable to receive the reply pointer.
Caller must free the returned reply with freeReplyObject unless automatic reply free is enabled.
Caller should check the integer return value for success/failure (exact values not specified here).

functions.name: redisAppendFormattedCommand
functions.signature: int redisAppendFormattedCommand(redisContext *c, const char *cmd, size_t len);
functions.description: Appends a preformatted RESP command buffer to the context’s output buffer for later write. Intended for building pipelines in blocking mode or queued writes in non-blocking mode.
requirements: c must be a valid redisContext.
cmd must point to a buffer containing a valid RESP command of length len.
Caller should check the integer return value for success/failure (exact values not specified here).

functions.name: redisvAppendCommand
functions.signature: int redisvAppendCommand(redisContext *c, const char *format, va_list ap);
functions.description: Formats a Redis command from a printf-like format string and va_list, and appends it to the context’s output buffer.
requirements: c must be a valid redisContext.
format must be a valid hiredis command format string; ap must match the format.
Caller should check the integer return value for success/failure (exact values not specified here).

functions.name: redisAppendCommand
functions.description: Formats a Redis command from a printf-like format string and variadic arguments, and appends it to the context’s output buffer. Useful for pipelining.
requirements: c must be a valid redisContext.
format must be a valid hiredis command format string matching the provided arguments.
Caller should check the integer return value for success/failure (exact values not specified here).

functions.name: redisAppendCommandArgv
functions.signature: int redisAppendCommandArgv(redisContext *c, int argc, const char **argv, const size_t *argvlen);
functions.description: Formats a Redis command from an argument vector (argc/argv) and appends it to the context’s output buffer.
requirements: c must be a valid redisContext.
argc should match the number of entries in argv and argvlen (if provided).
argv must point to argc argument strings; if argvlen is provided, each length corresponds to the respective argv entry.
Caller should check the integer return value for success/failure (exact values not specified here).

functions.name: redisvCommand
functions.description: Issues a command to Redis using a printf-like format string and va_list. In blocking mode, appends the command and reads a reply, returning a reply object; in non-blocking mode, appends the command and returns NULL.
requirements: c must be a valid redisContext.
format must be a valid hiredis command format string; ap must match the format.
In blocking mode, caller must free the returned reply with freeReplyObject. In non-blocking mode, the return is always NULL.
Caller must check c->err/errstr on errors (function may return NULL on error even in blocking mode).

functions.name: redisCommand
functions.description: Issues a command to Redis using a printf-like format string and variadic arguments. In blocking mode, returns a reply object; in non-blocking mode, queues the command and returns NULL.
requirements: c must be a valid redisContext.
format must be a valid hiredis command format string matching the provided arguments.
In blocking mode, caller must free the returned reply with freeReplyObject. In non-blocking mode, the return is always NULL.
Caller must check c->err/errstr on errors (function may return NULL on error even in blocking mode).

functions.name: redisCommandArgv
functions.signature: void *redisCommandArgv(redisContext *c, int argc, const char **argv, const size_t *argvlen);
functions.description: Issues a command to Redis from an argument vector (argc/argv). In blocking mode, returns a reply object; in non-blocking mode, queues the command and returns NULL.
requirements: c must be a valid redisContext.
argc should match the number of entries in argv and argvlen (if provided).
argv must point to argc argument strings; if argvlen is provided, each length corresponds to the respective argv entry.
In blocking mode, caller must free the returned reply with freeReplyObject. In non-blocking mode, the return is always NULL.
Caller must check c->err/errstr on errors (function may return NULL on error even in blocking mode).

functions.name: redisAsyncConnectWithOptions
functions.description: Create a new asynchronous Redis connection using a filled redisOptions structure. Intended for configuring TCP, Unix socket, timeouts, and other options before connecting. Returns a redisAsyncContext pointer on success or NULL/errored context on failure.
requirements: options must point to a valid, initialized redisOptions struct appropriate for hiredis (exact required fields are defined with redisOptions elsewhere).
The returned redisAsyncContext must be integrated with an event loop before I/O will progress (via the ev hooks).
Caller should check the returned context’s err/errstr fields or NULL to determine if the connection failed.
The context must later be disconnected/freed with redisAsyncDisconnect/redisAsyncFree.

functions.name: redisAsyncConnect
functions.description: Create a new asynchronous TCP connection to a Redis server at the specified IPv4/IPv6 textual address and port. Returns a redisAsyncContext on success or a context/NULL indicating failure.
requirements: ip must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated string containing a valid IP address or resolvable hostname.
port must be in the valid TCP port range (1–65535).
The returned context must be attached to an event loop to drive I/O (using the ev hooks).
Caller should inspect the returned context’s err/errstr or NULL to detect connection errors.
Free/disconnect the context with redisAsyncDisconnect/redisAsyncFree when finished.

functions.name: redisAsyncConnectBind
functions.signature: redisAsyncContext *redisAsyncConnectBind(const char *ip, int port, const char *source_addr);
functions.description: Create a new asynchronous TCP connection to a Redis server, binding the local socket to source_addr before connecting. Useful for selecting the outgoing interface/address.
requirements: ip must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated string containing a valid remote address/hostname.
port must be in range 1–65535.
source_addr must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated string with a valid local address parseable by the OS.
Attach the returned context to an event loop for I/O to progress.
Check the returned context’s err/errstr or NULL to detect connection errors.
Disconnect/free the context when done.

functions.name: redisAsyncConnectBindWithReuse
functions.signature: redisAsyncContext *redisAsyncConnectBindWithReuse(const char *ip, int port, const char *source_addr);
functions.description: Create a new asynchronous TCP connection to a Redis server, binding to source_addr with address-reuse enabled (e.g., SO_REUSEADDR) before connecting. Helps when rebinding recently used local addresses.
requirements: ip must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated string.
port must be 1–65535.
source_addr must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated string containing a valid local address.
Attach the returned context to an event loop to handle read/write events.
Check the context’s err/errstr or NULL for connection errors.
Disconnect/free the context when finished.

functions.name: redisAsyncConnectUnix
functions.description: Create a new asynchronous Unix domain socket connection to a Redis server listening on the given filesystem path.
requirements: path must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated string naming a valid Unix socket path.
The returned context must be attached to an event loop to progress I/O.
Caller should check err/errstr or NULL to detect connection errors.
Disconnect/free the context when done.

functions.name: redisAsyncSetConnectCallback
functions.description: Register a callback to be invoked when the first write event (indicating connection progress/completion) occurs on the async context. The callback receives the context and a status code.
requirements: ac must be a valid, non-NULL redisAsyncContext created by one of the redisAsyncConnect* functions and not yet freed.
fn must be a valid function pointer to a callback compatible with redisConnectCallback (const redisAsyncContext*, int).
Caller should check the integer return value to determine success/failure (exact codes defined by hiredis).
Set the callback before or during connection setup so it can be triggered appropriately (exact timing semantics are library-defined).

functions.name: redisAsyncSetConnectCallbackNC
functions.description: Register a connect callback variant that receives a non-const redisAsyncContext* alongside a status code. Useful when the callback needs to modify the context.
requirements: ac must be a valid, non-NULL redisAsyncContext that has not been freed.
fn must be a valid function pointer compatible with redisConnectCallbackNC (redisAsyncContext*, int).
Caller should check the integer return value for success/failure.
Set before or during connection establishment so it can be invoked.

functions.name: redisAsyncSetDisconnectCallback

tv.tv_sec >= 0 and tv.tv_usec >= 0 (non-negative components).

import random
import struct
import string

# Generator for hiredis redisFormatCommand fuzzer stub.
# The stub will call FUZZ_PARAM_STR three times and select among 5 format cases.
# We must return a bytes buffer that the fuzzer framework will slice to serve
# FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int) and FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls. We craft the buffer so that
# each call receives valid, interesting values producing sensible commands.
#
# Assumed FUZZ_PARAM layout (common in fuzzing harnesses):
# - When an unsigned int is requested, the framework consumes 4 bytes little-endian.
# - When a string is requested, the framework consumes a length prefix and then bytes,
#   or it may scan for NUL terminator. We can't be certain. To be robust, we embed
#   multiple NUL-terminated strings back-to-back and also include length-prefixed
#   variants so either convention yields usable data. Many fuzzers use NUL-terminated
#   for FUZZ_PARAM_STR, so we ensure NULs are present and within limits.
#
# Strategy:
# - Emit a 4-byte choice selector to drive the switch (case 0..4).
# - Then for each of three strings, emit both a NUL-terminated view and a binary blob
#   the harness might choose from. The content is crafted to be valid Redis arguments
#   for commands issued in the stub: keys, values, field names, integers (for INCRBY key).
# - Keep total size <= 4096.
#
# String themes we generate:
# - Redis-safe ASCII keys (alnum, punctuation).
# - Binary-like payloads including spaces, newlines, and NULs kept after the first NUL
#   so C-string paths remain valid while %b variants can still consume lengths from s.data().
# - Special names like "key", "field", "hash", and variable randoms to vary coverage.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

ALNUM_PUNCT = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_:.@/[]{}()$#,+*=!" 

def _rand_ascii(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return ''.join(rng.choice(ALNUM_PUNCT) for _ in range(n))

def _rand_binary(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    # Mix printable and control bytes but keep at least one NUL not at the start.
    data = bytearray(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))
    if n > 2:
        pos = rng.randint(1, n-1)
        data[pos] = 0
    return bytes(data)

def _nul_terminated(b: bytes) -> bytes:
    # Ensure exactly one NUL terminator added (safe if already contains NUL earlier).
    if not b or b[-1] != 0:
        return b + b"\x00"
    return b

def _make_str_block(rng: random.Random, theme: str) -> bytes:
    # Create a block representing one FUZZ_PARAM_STR that is useful for both %s and %b uses.
    # Layout:
    # [ASCII c-string]\0 [binary payload length (LE32)] [binary payload bytes]
    # Many harnesses will only use the c-string portion; hiredis %b uses provided data/len
    # from the stub, not from our buffer, but we keep binary part to satisfy possible
    # length-prefixed consumers.
    if theme == 'key':
        base = rng.choice(['key', 'user', 'session', 'account', 'k']) + ':' + _rand_ascii(rng, 3, 12)
    elif theme == 'field':
        base = rng.choice(['field', 'col', 'attr', 'f']) + '_' + _rand_ascii(rng, 2, 10)
    elif theme == 'value':
        base = rng.choice(['val', 'json', 'blob', 'data']) + '-' + _rand_ascii(rng, 2, 8)
    elif theme == 'hash':
        base = 'hash:' + _rand_ascii(rng, 4, 10)
    elif theme == 'intlike':
        # For INCRBY key %lld, the key is s1.c_str(); we make it alnum so it's valid key.
        base = rng.choice(['counter', 'cnt', 'hits']) + ':' + _rand_ascii(rng, 2, 8)
    else:
        base = _rand_ascii(rng, 3, 16)

    cstr = _nul_terminated(base.encode('utf-8'))

    # Binary payload: build something different from cstr to exercise %b paths.
    bin_payload = _rand_binary(rng, 0, 64)
    # Sometimes embed textual JSON-like or spaces/newlines to test tokenization
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        extra = (rng.choice(['{"a":1}', '{"ok":true}', 'line1\nline2', 'value with spaces']).encode('utf-8'))
        # Keep first NUL early for C-string; append binary after it so %b will see full data
        bin_payload = (b"\x00" if rng.random() < 0.4 else b"") + extra + (b"\x00" if rng.random() < 0.3 else b"")
    le_len = struct.pack('<I', len(bin_payload))
    return cstr + le_len + bin_payload

def _build_case_selector(rng: random.Random) -> int:
    # Choose among 5 cases with some weighting to cover all
    weights = [1, 2, 2, 2, 2]  # include simple PING but favor others
    choices = []
    for i, w in enumerate(weights):
        choices.extend([i] * w)
    return rng.choice(choices)

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Select case for the first FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int)
    case = _build_case_selector(rng)
    buf = bytearray()
    buf += struct.pack('<I', case)

    # Build three FUZZ_PARAM_STR blocks tailored for each case to produce valid commands
    # case 0: PING ignores strings, but we still provide sensible data
    # case 1: GET %s -> s1 should be a key
    # case 2: SET %b %b -> s1 and s2 can be arbitrary/binary; we ensure non-empty sometimes
    # case 3: HSET %s %s %b -> s1 hash key, s2 field, s3 value (binary ok)
    # case 4: INCRBY %s %lld -> s1 key; we also need another FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int) for inc

    # s1
    theme1 = 'key' if case in (1, 4) else ('hash' if case == 3 else 'value')
    buf += _make_str_block(rng, theme1)

    # s2
    theme2 = 'value' if case == 2 else ('field' if case == 3 else 'value')
    buf += _make_str_block(rng, theme2)

    # s3
    theme3 = 'value'
    buf += _make_str_block(rng, theme3)

    # For default case in stub (case 4), it consumes another unsigned int to compute inc
    if case == 4:
        # Choose a range including negatives when cast to long long via modulo, but stub uses % 100000
        inc = rng.randrange(0, 200000)
        buf += struct.pack('<I', inc)

    # Bound the total size
    return bytes(buf[:MAX_TOTAL])

# Generator for Redis bulk-safe binary data to be used by hiredis redisFormatCommand fuzzer stub.
# The fuzzer stub requests three FUZZ_PARAM_STR strings (s1, s2, s3), each truncated to 1024 bytes.
# It then selects one of several command formatting patterns that use %s and %b (binary-safe) specifiers.
# Our goal is to return a single bytes buffer that the harness will split to feed FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls.
# We therefore pack multiple interesting byte sequences concatenated, letting the harness slice them
# deterministically. We keep total size <= 4096.

MAX_PART = 1024
MAX_TOTAL = 4096

ASCII_KEYS = [
    b"key",
    b"foo",
    b"bar",
    b"baz",
    b"long_key_name_with_namespace:sub:leaf",
    b"utf8:\xe2\x98\x83:snowman",  # UTF-8
    b"empty",  # sometimes empty will be separate variant
]

BINARY_PATTERNS = [
    # Pure binary with NULs and high bytes
    lambda rng, n: bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n)),
    # Repeating small pattern
    lambda rng, n: (b"\x00\xff\x7f\x80ABC\n\r\t" * (n // 9 + 1))[:n],
    # Incrementing bytes
    lambda rng, n: bytes((i % 256) for i in range(n)),
    # Zlib member (valid compressed stream)
    lambda rng, n: (zlib.compress(b"Z" * max(1, min(n, 512))) + b"X" * n)[:n],
    # Mixed text + NULs
    lambda rng, n: (b"value\x00with\x00nuls:" + bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(max(0, n-17))))[:n],
]

def _rand_len(rng: random.Random, max_len: int) -> int:
    # Bias lengths toward edge cases and a spread across the range
    choices = [0, 1, 2, 7, 8, 15, 16, 31, 32, 63, 64, 127, 128, 255, 256, 511, 512, 768, 1023, 1024]
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        return min(max_len, rng.choice(choices))
    # Otherwise uniform in range
    return rng.randrange(0, max_len + 1)

def _make_ascii_like(rng: random.Random, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    # Generate plausible key/field names (for %s cases): mix of predefined and random safe chars
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        base = rng.choice(ASCII_KEYS)
        extra_len = max(0, _rand_len(rng, max_len) - len(base))
        suffix = b""
        if extra_len > 0:
            pool = b"-_:.@/\"'[]{}()$%abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789"
            suffix = bytes(pool[rng.randrange(len(pool))] for _ in range(extra_len))
        out = (base + suffix)[:max_len]
        return out
    # random ascii-safe length up to max
    n = _rand_len(rng, max_len)
    pool = b"-_:.@/\"'[]{}()$%abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789"
    return bytes(pool[rng.randrange(len(pool))] for _ in range(n))

def _make_binary(rng: random.Random, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    n = _rand_len(rng, max_len)
    patt = rng.choice(BINARY_PATTERNS)
    return patt(rng, n)

def _ensure_nonempty_pref(rng: random.Random, b: bytes, fallback: bytes) -> bytes:
    if len(b) == 0:
        return fallback
    return b

def _compose_parts(parts):
    # Join and truncate to MAX_TOTAL
    data = b"".join(parts)
    return data[:MAX_TOTAL]

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # We craft three segments corresponding to s1, s2, s3 consumed by the stub.
    # To encourage coverage across switch cases, we mix ASCII-like and binary-safe payloads, including edge lengths.

    # s1 is frequently used as key name with %s and %b; prefer ASCII-like but sometimes binary
    if rng.random() < 0.75:
        s1 = _make_ascii_like(rng, MAX_PART)
        s1 = _ensure_nonempty_pref(rng, s1, b"key")
    else:
        s1 = _make_binary(rng, MAX_PART)
        s1 = _ensure_nonempty_pref(rng, s1, b"k")

    # s2 can be either value or field; mix texty and binary
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        s2 = _make_binary(rng, MAX_PART)
        s2 = _ensure_nonempty_pref(rng, s2, b"v")
    else:
        s2 = _make_ascii_like(rng, MAX_PART)
        s2 = _ensure_nonempty_pref(rng, s2, b"val")

    # s3 used as %b in HSET case; prefer more binary with embedded NULs
    s3 = _make_binary(rng, MAX_PART)
    s3 = _ensure_nonempty_pref(rng, s3, b"data")

    # Occasionally craft special interesting shapes
    # 1) Large near-1KB payloads
    if rng.random() < 0.2:
        s2 = BINARY_PATTERNS[2](rng, 1024)
    if rng.random() < 0.2:
        s3 = BINARY_PATTERNS[0](rng, 1024)
    # 2) Include exact edge sizes 0, 1, 1024 to check truncation behaviors
    if rng.random() < 0.1:
        s1 = s1[:0]
    if rng.random() < 0.1:
        s2 = s2[:1]
    if rng.random() < 0.1:
        s3 = s3[:1024]

    # Prepend a small header that might be consumed by the harness as non-string data
    # The stub first reads an unsigned int for choice; we supply 4 bytes up front so the
    # harness can deterministically read a value that influences the switch case.
    # Encode a biased choice cycling 0..4 for coverage.
    choice = rng.randrange(0, 5)
    header = struct.pack("<I", choice)

    # Concatenate header + s1 + s2 + s3; the harness will use them in sequence via FUZZ_PARAM*
    out = _compose_parts([header, s1, s2, s3])
    return out

import random
from typing import List

# This generator produces a single bytes buffer that the fuzzing harness will
# hand to FUZZ_PARAM_STR / FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME / FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int).
# We focus on generating valid and interesting Redis command argv elements
# (binary-safe), covering common commands and edge cases, while keeping inputs
# within 4096 bytes.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

# A small corpus of realistic Redis command argument vectors. We encode them
# as a single bytes blob that the harness will split into FUZZ_PARAM_STR pulls.
# Since the stubs fetch up to 4 strings per call, we pack multiple logical
# strings in one buffer using a simple length-prefixed format that typical
# fuzz harnesses can sample from. However, we cannot rely on harness decoding.
# Therefore we instead provide a flat bytes blob consisting of concatenated
# ASCII and binary chunks separated by random delimiters and nulls; most
# consumers will slice substrings from this buffer, yielding useful argv.

ASCII_COMMAND_SETS: List[List[bytes]] = [
    [b"PING"],
    [b"ECHO", b"Hello, world!"],
    [b"SET", b"mykey", b"myvalue"],
    [b"GET", b"mykey"],
    [b"DEL", b"mykey"],
    [b"INCR", b"counter"],
    [b"LPUSH", b"list", b"a", b"b"],
    [b"RPUSH", b"list", b"x", b"y", b"z"],
    [b"HSET", b"hash", b"field", b"val"],
    [b"HGET", b"hash", b"field"],
    [b"ZADD", b"z", b"1", b"a", b"2", b"b"],
    [b"ZINCRBY", b"z", b"2.5", b"member"],
    [b"MSET", b"k1", b"v1", b"k2", b"v2"],
    [b"SETEX", b"expkey", b"10", b"val"],
    [b"PSETEX", b"expkeyms", b"1500", b"val"],
    [b"SET", b"nxkey", b"nxval", b"NX"],
    [b"SET", b"xxkey", b"xxval", b"XX"],
    [b"SET", b"keepttl", b"v", b"KEEPTTL"],

    [b"APPEND", b"mykey", b"suffix"],
    [b"BITCOUNT", b"mykey"],

    [b"EVAL", b"return ARGV[1]", b"0", b"arg"],

    [b"GEOADD", b"geo", b"13.361389", b"38.115556", b"Palermo"],
    [b"XADD", b"stream", b"*", b"f", b"v"],
    [b"JSON.SET", b"doc", b"$", b"{\"a\":1}"],
]

# Binary payload makers for argvlen coverage (embedded NULs, high bytes, etc.)

def make_binary_blob(rnd: random.Random, min_len: int = 1, max_len: int = 256) -> bytes:
    n = rnd.randint(min_len, max_len)
    # Mix ASCII, NULs, and random bytes
    parts = []
    i = 0
    while i < n:
        choice = rnd.randint(0, 4)
        if choice == 0:
            # ASCII run
            run = rnd.randint(1, min(16, n - i))
            s = bytes(rnd.choice(b"ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789-_:") for _ in range(run))
            parts.append(s)
            i += run
        elif choice == 1:
            # NUL bytes
            run = rnd.randint(1, min(8, n - i))
            parts.append(b"\x00" * run)
            i += run
        else:
            # Raw random
            run = rnd.randint(1, min(16, n - i))
            parts.append(bytes(rnd.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(run)))
            i += run
    return b"".join(parts)

# Compose a buffer that contains multiple plausible argv strings concatenated
# with separators that allow the harness to extract diverse substrings when it
# calls FUZZ_PARAM_STR multiple times.

def compose_buffer(chunks: List[bytes], rnd: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Use a mix of separators including newlines, spaces, CRLF, and NULs.
    seps = [b"\n", b" ", b"\r\n", b"\x00", b"\t"]
    out = bytearray()
    for i, c in enumerate(chunks):
        out += c
        if i != len(chunks) - 1:
            # 1-3 separators
            for _ in range(rnd.randint(1, 3)):
                out += rnd.choice(seps)
    return bytes(out)

# Build a set of up to 4 arguments for the stubs that request up to 4 FUZZ_PARAM_STRs.

def build_argset(rnd: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    choice = rnd.random()
    args: List[bytes] = []
    if choice < 0.6:
        # Pick from known ASCII command sets
        cmd = rnd.choice(ASCII_COMMAND_SETS)
        args = list(cmd)
    else:
        # Construct a random command with binary-safe args
        verbs = [
            b"SET", b"GET", b"DEL", b"ECHO", b"INCR", b"LPUSH", b"RPUSH",
            b"HSET", b"HGET", b"ZADD", b"EVAL", b"XADD"
        ]
        argc = rnd.randint(1, 4)
        if argc >= 1:
            args.append(rnd.choice(verbs))
        for _ in range(argc - 1):
            # Mix of ascii and binary blobs
            if rnd.random() < 0.5:
                args.append(make_binary_blob(rnd, 1, 64))
            else:
                # short ascii token
                token_len = rnd.randint(1, 16)
                token = bytes(rnd.choice(b"ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789-_:") for _ in range(token_len))
                args.append(token)
    # Trim to 4 maximum
    return args[:4]

# Generate additional entropy buffer to satisfy FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int) consumption.
# Many harnesses will pull raw bytes; providing some random tail helps.

def make_uint_entropy(rnd: random.Random, count: int = 8) -> bytes:
    return b"".join((rnd.getrandbits(32)).to_bytes(4, "little") for _ in range(count))


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rnd = random.Random(seed)

    # Build one or two arg sets to populate enough material for multiple stubs.
    argsets = [build_argset(rnd)]
    if rnd.random() < 0.5:
        argsets.append(build_argset(rnd))

    chunks: List[bytes] = []
    # Interleave argument sets with occasional RESP-like fragments to exercise
    # formatted command expectations without relying on strict RESP framing.
    for args in argsets:
        # Add args
        chunks.extend(args)
        # Optionally add a RESP-like hint buffer
        if rnd.random() < 0.5:
            # Minimal RESP array for the first two args, e.g., *2\r\n$3\r\nGET\r\n$3\r\nkey\r\n
            a = args[:]
            if len(a) >= 1 and len(a[0]) > 0:
                # limit bulk lengths to not exceed MAX_TOTAL
                def bulk(b: bytes) -> bytes:
                    return b"$" + str(len(b)).encode() + b"\r\n" + b + b"\r\n"
                resp = bytearray()
                resp += b"*" + str(len(a)).encode() + b"\r\n"
                for part in a:
                    # Cap very large bulk to 128 to keep total under budget
                    p = part if len(part) <= 128 else part[:128]
                    resp += bulk(p)
                chunks.append(bytes(resp))

        # Add some binary blobs to force argvlen paths
        if rnd.random() < 0.7:
            chunks.append(make_binary_blob(rnd, 1, 64))

    # Compose base buffer
    buf = compose_buffer(chunks, rnd)

    # Append uint entropy and some extra separators
    tail = bytearray()
    tail += b"\r\n\n\x00"
    tail += make_uint_entropy(rnd, count=8)

    out = buf + bytes(tail)

    # Ensure size limit
    if len(out) > MAX_TOTAL:
        out = out[:MAX_TOTAL]

    # Guarantee non-empty
    if not out:
        out = b"PING\n"

    return out

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Generator for Filesystem path strings (NUL-terminated C-strings) suitable for Unix domain sockets
# and host/IP strings for TCP along with valid-looking ports encoded in the same buffer for the fuzzer
# to slice. We produce a bytes blob containing multiple NUL-terminated strings:
# - Several candidate Unix socket paths
# - Several candidate host/IP strings
# The fuzzer stub will request either FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME (for Unix socket path) or FUZZ_PARAM_STR (for IP/host).
# We therefore pack diverse, valid-looking values to increase coverage.
#
# Constraints:
# - Total size <= 4096 bytes
# - No I/O, deterministic given seed, but with randomness per call
# - Strings are likely valid, not malformed

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

def _rand_choice(rng: random.Random, items: List[str]) -> str:
    return items[rng.randrange(len(items))]

def _rand_ipv4(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Mix of private, loopback, multicast, and public-looking ranges
    choices = [
        ("127", rng.randrange(0, 256), rng.randrange(0, 256), rng.randrange(1, 255)),
        ("10", rng.randrange(0, 256), rng.randrange(0, 256), rng.randrange(1, 255)),
        ("172", rng.randrange(16, 32), rng.randrange(0, 256), rng.randrange(1, 255)),
        ("192", 168, rng.randrange(0, 256), rng.randrange(1, 255)),
        (str(rng.randrange(1, 223)), rng.randrange(0, 256), rng.randrange(0, 256), rng.randrange(1, 255)),
    ]
    a,b,c,d = _rand_choice(rng, choices)
    return f"{a}.{b}.{c}.{d}"

def _rand_hostname(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Generate a plausible hostname with labels 1-4, 1-15 chars each
    labels = []
    nlabels = rng.randint(1, 4)
    alphabet = string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits
    for _ in range(nlabels):
        ln = rng.randint(1, 15)
        # labels should start/end alnum and can include hyphen inside
        core = ''.join(rng.choice(alphabet + '-') for _ in range(ln))
        core = core.strip('-') or 'a'
        labels.append(core)
    return '.'.join(labels)

def _rand_ipv6(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Compact IPv6 forms are tricky; provide common patterns and full form
    def hextet():
        return format(rng.randrange(0, 0x10000), 'x')
    patterns = []
    # Full form
    patterns.append(':'.join(hextet() for _ in range(8)))
    # With :: compression at random position
    pos = rng.randrange(0, 7)
    left = [hextet() for _ in range(pos)]
    right = [hextet() for _ in range(7 - pos)]
    patterns.append((':'.join(left) if left else '') + '::' + (':'.join(right) if right else ''))
    # IPv4-mapped
    patterns.append('::ffff:' + _rand_ipv4(rng))
    return _rand_choice(rng, patterns)

def _rand_port(rng: random.Random) -> int:
    # Valid TCP port 1..65535
    return rng.randint(1, 65535)

def _unix_paths(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    # Common Unix socket locations and random temp-like paths
    candidates = [
        "/var/run/redis/redis.sock",
        "/tmp/redis.sock",
        "/run/redis/redis-server.sock",
        "/var/tmp/redis.sock",
    ]
    # Generate several randomized candidates under /tmp and nested directories
    for _ in range(rng.randint(3, 8)):
        prefix = _rand_choice(rng, ["/tmp", "/var/run", "/run", "/private/tmp"]) \
                 + '/' + ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_lowercase) for _ in range(rng.randint(3,10)))
        name = _rand_choice(rng, ["redis.sock", "redis-server.sock", ".redis.sock"]) if rng.random() < 0.7 else \
               ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_lowercase+string.digits+"._-") for _ in range(rng.randint(3,16)))
        candidates.append(prefix + '/' + name)
    # Paths within user home-like
    for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 3)):
        dirn = '/home/' + ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_lowercase) for _ in range(rng.randint(3,8)))
        candidates.append(dirn + '/.redis/redis.sock')
    return candidates

def _host_strings(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    hosts = [
        "localhost",
        "redis",
        _rand_ipv4(rng),
        _rand_hostname(rng),
        _rand_ipv6(rng),
        "::1",
        "127.0.0.1",
    ]
    # Add a few more random hostnames/IPs
    for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 5)):
        hosts.append(_rand_ipv4(rng))
    for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 3)):
        hosts.append(_rand_hostname(rng))
    return hosts

def _build_bytes_z(strings: List[str]) -> bytes:
    # Join as NUL-terminated C strings in one buffer; consumers can read one at a time
    # Ensure we do not exceed MAX_TOTAL
    out = bytearray()
    for s in strings:
        b = s.encode('utf-8', 'strict') + b"\x00"
        if len(out) + len(b) > MAX_TOTAL:
            break
        out += b
    return bytes(out)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Decide whether to target Unix sockets or TCP for this buffer build; include both to be safe
    paths = _unix_paths(rng)
    hosts = _host_strings(rng)

    # Mix in host:port strings as they are commonly used in tests, though stub separates them.
    # Still useful if consumer treats whole string as FUZZ_PARAM_STR.
    hostports = []
    for h in hosts:
        # Avoid embedding colons in IPv6 host:port directly; wrap in brackets when needed
        if ':' in h and not (h.startswith('[') and h.endswith(']')):
            hp = f"[{h}]:{_rand_port(rng)}"
        else:
            hp = f"{h}:{_rand_port(rng)}"
        hostports.append(hp)

    # Create a prioritized list: socket paths first (for FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME), then plain hosts, then host:port
    strings: List[str] = []
    # Ensure first entries are very common successful defaults
    strings.extend([
        "/tmp/redis.sock",
        "localhost",
        "127.0.0.1",
        "::1",
    ])

    # Add randomized sets
    # Shuffle to diversify ordering while keeping deterministic under seed
    rng.shuffle(paths)
    rng.shuffle(hosts)
    rng.shuffle(hostports)

    strings.extend(paths)
    strings.extend(hosts)
    strings.extend(hostports)

    # Truncate to not exceed budget when encoded
    data = _build_bytes_z(strings)

    # Guarantee non-empty and within limit
    if not data:
        data = b"/tmp/redis.sock\x00localhost\x00"
    return data

# - SET <key> <val>
# - GET <key>
# - INCR <key>
# - LPUSH <list> <val>
# - HSET <hash> <field> <val>
# - DEL <key>
# - EXPIRE <key> <seconds>
# - CLIENT ID (no args variant to test zero bulk besides command)
# All are encoded as RESP arrays with bulk strings.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096
MAX_ARG = 128

_SIMPLE_COMMANDS = [
    ("PING", []),
    ("CLIENT", ["ID"]),
]

def _rand_ascii(r: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    length = r.randint(min_len, max_len)
    # Use a mix of safe ASCII including spaces and punctuation, but avoid CR/LF inside bulk data.
    alphabet = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789 _-.:@/+#?=,"
    return "".join(r.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(length))

def _bounded_arg(s: str) -> str:
    if len(s) > MAX_ARG:
        return s[:MAX_ARG]
    return s

def _resp_encode(argv: List[bytes]) -> bytes:
    # Encode as: *<argc>\r\n$<len>\r\n<data>\r\n ...
    parts: List[bytes] = []
    parts.append(b"*" + str(len(argv)).encode("ascii") + b"\r\n")
    for a in argv:
        parts.append(b"$" + str(len(a)).encode("ascii") + b"\r\n")
        parts.append(a + b"\r\n")
    return b"".join(parts)

def _build_command(r: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    choice = r.randint(0, 9)
    # Ensure non-empty key/val where required
    if choice == 0:
        # PING
        return ["PING"]
    elif choice == 1:
        # ECHO <msg>
        msg = _bounded_arg(_rand_ascii(r, 1, 20))
        return ["ECHO", msg]
    elif choice == 2:
        # SET <key> <val>
        key = _bounded_arg(_rand_ascii(r, 1, 16))
        val = _bounded_arg(_rand_ascii(r, 1, 32))
        return ["SET", key, val]
    elif choice == 3:
        # GET <key>
        key = _bounded_arg(_rand_ascii(r, 1, 16))
        return ["GET", key]
    elif choice == 4:
        # INCR <key>
        key = _bounded_arg(_rand_ascii(r, 1, 16))
        return ["INCR", key]
    elif choice == 5:
        # LPUSH <list> <val>
        lst = _bounded_arg(_rand_ascii(r, 1, 16))
        val = _bounded_arg(_rand_ascii(r, 1, 24))
        return ["LPUSH", lst, val]
    elif choice == 6:
        # HSET <hash> <field> <val>
        h = _bounded_arg(_rand_ascii(r, 1, 16))
        f = _bounded_arg(_rand_ascii(r, 1, 16))
        v = _bounded_arg(_rand_ascii(r, 1, 24))
        return ["HSET", h, f, v]
    elif choice == 7:
        # DEL <key>
        key = _bounded_arg(_rand_ascii(r, 1, 16))
        return ["DEL", key]
    elif choice == 8:
        # EXPIRE <key> <seconds>
        key = _bounded_arg(_rand_ascii(r, 1, 16))
        seconds = str(r.randint(1, 600))
        return ["EXPIRE", key, seconds]
    else:
        # CLIENT ID
        return ["CLIENT", "ID"]

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)

    # Build one command; keep size small and valid.
    argv_str = _build_command(r)

    # Ensure arguments respect size constraints and avoid CR/LF inside bulk data
    safe_args: List[bytes] = []
    for s in argv_str:
        if not isinstance(s, str):
            s = str(s)
        # Strip CR/LF to maintain RESP validity
        s = s.replace("\r", " ").replace("\n", " ")
        s = _bounded_arg(s)
        safe_args.append(s.encode("utf-8", errors="strict"))

    resp = _resp_encode(safe_args)

    # Final guardrails
    if not resp or len(resp) > MAX_TOTAL:
        # Fallback to a minimal valid command
        resp = _resp_encode([b"PING"])
    return resp
